tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a plant wide solids inventory survey across liquid and solids trains.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: survey covers aeration trains, clarifiers, digesters, and storage on one day at a large plant.

cards.label: Plan the survey day for a normal loading day and brief samplers on points and methods
Calculate the mass held in each vessel and total the plant inventory
Correct the control method by the survey difference and file the survey as the new reference
Compare the survey total with the running process control inventory estimate
Measure volumes and levels in every vessel holding solids on the survey morning
Sample solids concentration at every survey point within the same few hours

tasks.explanation: Points and methods are fixed before sampling so results are comparable, masses are calculated from same day volumes and concentrations, and the survey resets the control estimate.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for verifying automatic wasting control against manual mass checks.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: waste pumps run on automatic flow paced control, senior operator wants a monthly verification.

cards.label: Sample waste sludge concentration on the same days as the flow checks
Download the automatic wasting volumes and flow records for the verification week
Correct the automatic factor or repair the meter if the two methods disagree beyond tolerance
File the verification and schedule the next one in the maintenance program
Measure actual waste flow by drawdown or timed volume on each waste line
Calculate mass wasted by the manual method and by the automatic records

tasks.explanation: Manual measurement is the reference the automation is judged against, mass needs both flow and concentration, and correction follows only a proven disagreement.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for resetting solids retention time targets after a new treatment train is commissioned.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: plant capacity has grown by one train, historic wasting rates no longer fit the larger inventory volume.

cards.label: Brief all shifts on the new targets, rates, and the reason they changed
Run the expanded plant for a month with weekly inventory and nutrient reviews
Calculate the new total aeration and clarifier volume in service with all trains online
Work out the wasting rates that hold the new inventory at current loadings
Confirm or revise the targets at the monthly review and update the control plan
Set the target inventory mass for the expanded plant from the seasonal retention time targets

tasks.explanation: New volumes change every rate, so targets are recalculated before shifts are briefed, and a month of weekly reviews confirms the new numbers in practice.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a digester loading optimization review.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: two primary digesters, feed rates have crept up, gas production per unit feed has fallen.

cards.label: Rebalance feed between the digesters toward the better performing loading
Total volatile solids fed to each digester over the last month from feed records
Calculate the loading rate and retention time for each digester at its working volume
Record the loading that gave the best reduction and gas yield in the digestion plan
Compare gas production and volatile solids reduction between the digesters
Hold the new split for a month with weekly volatile acids and alkalinity checks

tasks.explanation: Loadings are calculated from records before feed is rebalanced, chemistry is watched through the trial month, and the best loading becomes the recorded standard.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for planning a co digestion trial with a high strength organic waste.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a food processing waste is offered as co feed, trial will run on one digester with the second as control.

cards.label: Characterize the waste for solids, strength, and any material that could upset digestion or dewatering
Raise the share in steps only if the trial digester stays stable and dewatering is unaffected
Track gas, volatile acids to alkalinity, and dewatering results on both digesters weekly
Feed the trial digester at the starting share while the control digester stays on sludge only
Calculate a starting co feed share that raises loading by only a small step
Confirm receiving, storage, and feed arrangements keep the waste separate and measurable

tasks.explanation: The waste is characterized before it is accepted, a control digester makes the trial readable, and the share rises only on proven stability.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for optimizing biogas use between the boiler and the cogeneration unit.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: plant produces more gas in summer than the boiler needs, cogeneration unit can take the surplus.

cards.label: Monitor gas storage, pressure, and flare operation daily through the change
Set the priority order so digester heating is secured before other uses take gas
Confirm digester heating demand for the coming season from temperature records
Adjust the cogeneration feed to take the surplus above heating needs
Total gas production and gas use by each consumer over the last month
Record the seasonal priority settings in the gas utilization plan

tasks.explanation: Production and heating demand are totalled before priorities change, heating is secured first because digestion depends on it, and flare and pressure checks guard the new split.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a digester mixing optimization study.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: temperature varies with depth in one digester, grit is accumulating, mixing schedule is under review.

cards.label: Review mixer run hours and the current mixing schedule against the profile results
Sample solids at the same points to find dead zones where solids are settling
Profile temperature at several depths and points in the digester on the same day
Keep the schedule that gives the most even profile and record it in the digestion plan
Repeat the temperature and solids profile after two weeks on the new schedule
Trial a revised mixing schedule with longer or reordered mixing periods

tasks.explanation: Profiles locate the dead zones before the schedule changes, the same profile judges the trial, and the winning schedule is recorded as the standard.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for optimizing digester heating control through a cold season.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: western Canadian winter, heating fuel use is high, digester temperature swings with feed changes.

cards.label: Record the winter heating settings and fuel use for the annual energy review
Track temperature stability and volatile acids weekly through the cold period
Check heat exchanger and recirculation operation for fouling or short cycling
Adjust heating control to hold the band and alarm on drift beyond it
Set a narrow temperature band and a steady feed schedule to reduce thermal shocks
Review digester temperature swings and heating fuel use from the previous winter

tasks.explanation: Last winter evidence and equipment checks come before settings change, steady feeding supports steady temperature, and weekly chemistry confirms stability.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a volatile solids reduction improvement program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: reduction is below the plant target, feed blending and retention time are the levers available.

cards.label: Hold the change for a full digester retention time before judging the result
Recalculate reduction from the next full month of mass data
Calculate current reduction from a full month of feed and digested sludge mass data
Review feed blend, loading, temperature, and mixing for the factor most limiting reduction
Keep the change if reduction improved and record the new feed practice in the plan
Correct the limiting factor in one change, such as rebalancing primary and waste sludge feed

tasks.explanation: A full month of mass data sets the true starting point, one factor changes at a time, and judgement waits for a full retention time to pass.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for investigating digester foaming at a large plant.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: foam is rising in one digester, gas pressure is fluctuating, feed includes waste activated sludge.

cards.label: Examine feed and digester samples microscopically for filamentous organisms carried from the liquid train
Check mixing and feed distribution for dead zones where foam can build
Review recent feed changes, loading, and temperature for events that match the foam start
Reduce feed to the foaming digester in one step and shift load to the stable digester
Apply the matched control, such as foam wasting or a liquid train filament correction, with senior approval
Track foam level, gas pressure, and chemistry daily until the digester is stable

tasks.explanation: Feed history and microscopy point to the source before load is shifted, the control matches the cause, and daily tracking proves stability before normal loading resumes.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for recovering a sour digester with a high volatile acids to alkalinity ratio.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: ratio is well above the normal band, gas production and methane content are falling.

cards.label: Confirm the condition with a repeat sample and check temperature for a heating failure
Restart feeding at a low rate and raise it in steps only as the ratio returns to the normal band
Stop or sharply reduce feed to the sour digester and shift essential feed to the healthy digester
Add alkalinity only on a calculated dose with senior approval if pH is falling
Resample volatile acids and alkalinity every few days and watch for the ratio turning down
Hold mixing gentle and steady to keep the remaining biomass in contact with the contents

tasks.explanation: Confirmation and heating checks come before feed is stopped, alkalinity is a calculated intervention not a reflex, and refeeing waits for the ratio to recover.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for optimizing the blend of primary sludge and waste activated sludge fed to digestion.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: feed blend has drifted toward waste sludge, gas yield and thickening performance have slipped.

cards.label: Verify the delivered blend with daily feed sampling for the first week
Track gas production per unit volatile solids fed through the next month
Calculate the blend that restores the target volatile solids mix from the digestion plan
Adjust thickener and primary pumping schedules to deliver the target blend
Record the blend and schedules that restored gas yield in the digestion plan
Analyse recent feed samples for the share and solids of each sludge stream

tasks.explanation: The delivered blend is measured before it is corrected, schedules deliver the target, and gas per unit fed judges whether the blend is right.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a senior gas system safety and utilization check.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: monthly senior check covers gas piping, condensate traps, pressure relief, flare, and storage.

cards.label: Confirm flare pilot, ignition, and flame monitoring are operating correctly
Log the check, raise work orders for any fault, and brief the next senior operator
Check gas storage level controls and high level alarms by simulation where the procedure allows
Test pressure relief and vacuum protection devices against the maintenance schedule
Review gas production, use, and flare records for the month for unexplained losses
Inspect condensate traps and low points and drain them in the set order

tasks.explanation: Records focus the inspection, condensate and relief devices protect the whole system, and every fault leaves as a work order with a briefed handover.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for planning digester cleaning and return to service to gain the most process benefit.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one digester is due for cleaning, the other must carry the full solids load for a month.

cards.label: Calculate whether the remaining digester can hold loading and retention time limits alone
Measure grit and inventory in the digester and confirm cleaning is still the right scope
Clean, inspect, and repair the vessel and record its true working volume
Reseed with active digested sludge and restart heating and mixing before feeding
Ramp feed in steps with daily chemistry until the digester carries its normal share
Draw down and transfer digestible contents to the operating digester before emptying

tasks.explanation: Capacity alone is proven before the vessel is emptied, active contents are saved for reseeding, and the ramp is guarded by daily chemistry.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a biosolids storage and inventory management program through winter.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: hauling is limited in deep winter, storage must hold several months of cake production.

cards.label: Measure available storage volume and the months of production it can hold
Confirm storage drainage, odour control, and access for winter loading are ready
Set the hauling schedule that keeps storage below the safe level before freeze up
Review the program each spring and adjust production or hauling assumptions
Track stored volume monthly and trigger extra hauling before the limit is reached
Calculate monthly cake production from dewatering records for the last year

tasks.explanation: Production and volume are calculated before the hauling schedule is set, readiness is checked before winter closes in, and monthly tracking triggers action before storage is full.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a centrifuge optimization trial on digested sludge.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: trial varies polymer dose, feed rate, and machine settings on one centrifuge over two weeks.

cards.label: Change one setting at a time, starting with polymer dose, and run long enough to reach steady cake
Compare settings on cake solids, capture, and polymer cost per unit of dry solids
Test feed rate and machine settings in the same one at a time pattern
Sample cake and centrate at each setting and record throughput for the run
Set the best combination as the standard and record it on the machine operating sheet
Record baseline cake solids, capture, polymer use, and centrate quality at current settings

tasks.explanation: Baselines and one at a time changes make the comparison fair, cake and centrate are judged together, and cost per dry unit decides the winner.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for selecting a dewatering polymer by laboratory and full scale testing.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: current polymer price has risen, two alternatives will be screened for the centrifuge program.

cards.label: Run each shortlisted polymer at full scale for several runs at its best laboratory dose
Compare cake solids, capture, and dose cost between the full scale runs
Award the program to the best overall product and set its starting dose in the procedure
Shortlist the best two products and confirm supply, storage, and make down requirements
Screen candidate polymers in the laboratory for floc formation, drainage, and shear resistance
Collect a representative digested sludge sample and record its solids and condition

tasks.explanation: Laboratory screening narrows the field before machine time is spent, full scale runs decide on real cake and capture, and the starting dose is set from those runs.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a cake solids improvement program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: cake solids have slipped two points over a season, hauling costs are rising with wet cake.

cards.label: Verify cake sampling and laboratory method so the slip is proven real, not a measurement change
Check machine wear items and polymer make down strength against their schedules
Correct the most likely cause and run a week of close cake sampling
Review feed solids, blend, and digestion performance for a change that wets the cake
Record the cause and the restored cake target in the dewatering log
Compare the recovery week with the slip period at similar feed conditions

tasks.explanation: Measurement is verified before the process is blamed, feed and machine causes are checked in order, and the recovery is proven at similar feed conditions.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for managing centrate quality so its return does not upset nutrient removal.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: centrate returns to the head of the plant with a high ammonia load, dewatering runs in campaigns.

cards.label: Consider returning centrate during high influent flow periods when the plant has spare capacity
Record the campaign schedule and its ammonia evidence in the nutrient control plan
Sample centrate for ammonia and solids across a full dewatering campaign
Calculate the ammonia load returned per hour at the current campaign schedule
Sample effluent ammonia on campaign days to confirm the new schedule protects nitrification
Reschedule dewatering to spread the return load across the day where storage allows

tasks.explanation: The returned load is measured before the schedule changes, spreading the load uses plant capacity fairly, and effluent ammonia proves the protection works.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for optimizing the dewatering schedule against digestion output and hauling.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: dewatering, digester withdrawal, storage, and hauling are planned together weekly by the senior operator.

cards.label: Confirm hauling bookings and the cake volume they will remove
Set the dewatering run hours that clear the ready sludge without overfilling storage
Sequence digester withdrawals so dewatering feed stays steady in solids and temperature
Run the schedule and record actual cake, centrate, and run hours daily
Review variances at the weekly meeting and adjust next week hours accordingly
Total digested sludge ready for dewatering and the storage space available this week

tasks.explanation: Ready sludge and hauling set the hours, steady feed protects cake quality, and weekly variance review keeps the joint schedule honest.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a dewatering equipment performance audit.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: annual audit covers feed pumps, polymer system, centrifuges, conveyors, and cake handling.

cards.label: Raise work orders for wear faults and procedure updates for practice faults
Run a witnessed performance test at the standard feed rate on each machine
Compare test results with the compiled year data to separate wear from operating practice
Compile a year of cake, capture, polymer, energy, and downtime data by machine
Issue the audit summary with the next year maintenance priorities
Inspect wear items, guards, wash systems, and instrumentation against the manual schedules

tasks.explanation: A year of data frames the audit, witnessed tests separate machine condition from practice, and findings leave as either work orders or procedure changes.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for controlling sidestream nutrient returns from solids handling.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: returns include centrate, thickener overflow, and storage drainage, all reaching the liquid train.

cards.label: Apply the selected control, such as equalized return timing, and hold other returns steady
Calculate each stream share of the total nitrogen and phosphorus load on the liquid train
Measure flow and nutrient strength of each return stream over a representative week
Record the load relief achieved and add return stream checks to the monthly balance
Identify the stream where timing or treatment gives the largest load relief
Resample the controlled stream and effluent nutrients through the next month

tasks.explanation: Each stream is measured before one is chosen for control, the largest relief is targeted first, and the monthly balance keeps the gain visible.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for winter dewatering and cake handling readiness.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: cake pad and loading area are outdoors, deep cold affects polymer make down and hauling.

cards.label: Brief crews on ice management around the pad and on cold start machine checks
Run a trial load out in the first cold week and correct any handling problem found
Agree the cold snap hauling plan and the storage trigger levels with the hauler
Stock critical spares and winter grade consumables for the dewatering machines
Confirm polymer storage and make down lines are protected from freezing
Inspect cake pad drainage, lighting, and loader access before freeze up

tasks.explanation: Readiness is checked before freeze up, not during the first cold snap, triggers are agreed with the hauler in advance, and a trial load proves the plan.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a screw press optimization review at a plant that dewaters undigested sludge.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: screw press dewaters thickened waste sludge, cake and wash water use are under review.

cards.label: Select the settings that balance cake, throughput, and water use for this sludge
Record baseline cake solids, throughput, polymer dose, and wash water use for a normal week
Trial press speed and polymer dose changes one at a time with cake sampling each run
Compare wash water and energy use between the trial settings
Update the machine operating sheet and the wash schedule with the selected settings
Check screen condition, flocculation tank mixing, and feed consistency for faults

tasks.explanation: Faults are ruled out before settings are trialled, one change at a time keeps results readable, and the balance point is recorded on the operating sheet.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for investigating poor solids capture in dewatering.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: centrate solids are high, the returned solids load is visibly raising influent strength.

cards.label: Review feed rate and feed solids for operation beyond the machine rating
Inspect machine internals for wear or damage that passes solids
Record the capture standard and add centrate solids to the weekly checks
Confirm capture with paired feed and centrate solids samples and a mass calculation
Correct the proven cause and rerun the paired sampling to verify capture
Check polymer dose, make down strength, and injection point for a delivery fault

tasks.explanation: Capture is proven by mass, not by appearance, delivery and loading faults are checked before internals, and verification sampling closes the investigation.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for reviewing the effluent compliance sampling program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: senior review checks sampling points, frequencies, and lab methods against provincial requirements and federal effluent limits.

cards.label: Compare the plant sampling schedule line by line with that requirement list
Verify sampler and analyser calibration records for the compliance points
Correct any gap in frequency, point, or method and brief the samplers
Check sample handling, preservation, and holding times against the laboratory method sheets
List every compliance parameter, sampling point, and frequency required for the plant
File the reviewed program and set the date for the next senior review

tasks.explanation: Requirements are listed before the schedule is judged, handling and calibration are checked with the schedule, and the filed review sets the next check date.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for responding to an effluent limit exceedance as the senior operator.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: a routine effluent sample exceeds a limit, verification and notification are urgent.

cards.label: Confirm the result with a repeat sample and check for a laboratory or sampling error
Review plant operating records for the day to find the cause of the exceedance
Take the immediate corrective action that stops further out of limit discharge if possible
File the event, cause, and corrective actions in the plant record for the regulator file
Increase effluent sampling until results return to compliance and stay there
Notify the supervisor and follow the reporting procedure for the exceedance

tasks.explanation: Confirmation comes before notification so the report is accurate, stopping the discharge comes before root cause work, and increased sampling proves the return to compliance.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for an ultraviolet disinfection optimization program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: ultraviolet system treats final effluent, lamp age and water clarity vary through the year.

cards.label: Sample effluent microbiology weekly under the new cleaning and dose settings
Clean and inspect lamps and sleeves and verify dose monitoring is calibrated
Record the seasonal settings and the evidence that they hold disinfection performance
Set the dose control and lamp cleaning frequency that holds the target dose in low clarity periods
Measure ultraviolet transmittance of the effluent through the operating range
Record lamp hours, dose, and effluent quality for the last year by season

tasks.explanation: A year of seasonal data frames the program, lamps and transmittance are proven before dose control is set, and microbiology sampling judges the result.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for optimizing chlorine disinfection of final effluent.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: effluent is disinfected with chlorine, residual and contact time targets apply.

cards.label: Measure effluent demand and residual across the flow range with a bench series
Set the flow paced dose range that holds the target residual without over chlorinating
Sample effluent microbiology and residual daily for two weeks at the new settings
Verify contact time at peak and average flow from tank volumes and flow records
Record the dose range and the contact time evidence in the disinfection plan
Check dechlorination, where used, so residual does not harm the receiving water

tasks.explanation: Demand and contact time are measured before the dose is set, dechlorination is part of the optimization, and two weeks of sampling proves the settings.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for responding to an effluent suspended solids excursion.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: final effluent solids rise sharply, clarifiers are suspect, limits still apply.

cards.label: Hold wasting steady to avoid adding to the solids load on the clarifiers
Resample effluent solids hourly until they return to the normal range
Confirm the excursion with repeat sampling and check sampler and laboratory results
Adjust return rate or flow split in one step to lower the blanket
Profile clarifier blanket depth and check for a rising or uneven blanket
Check return sludge rate, flow distribution, and scraper and drive operation

tasks.explanation: Sampling confirms the excursion, blanket and return checks locate the cause, and hourly resampling proves the recovery before routine sampling resumes.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for an effluent quality trending and early warning program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: senior operator wants trend charts that flag a quality drift before a limit is approached.

cards.label: Review warning accuracy quarterly and adjust levels that warn too late or too often
Compile two years of results and set the normal band and the early warning level for each parameter
Escalate a flagged drift to the senior operator the same day it is seen
Flag any three point drift toward a limit and note the operating conditions that day
Select the key effluent parameters and the control chart format for each one
Enter new results on the charts on the day they arrive, not at month end

tasks.explanation: Bands come from real history, daily entry keeps warnings timely, and quarterly review tunes levels that cry wolf or warn too late.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for managing a planned bypass or blending event and its reporting.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: maintenance forces a short planned bypass, provincial notification and reporting requirements apply in general terms.

cards.label: Notify the supervisor and follow the reporting and notification procedure for the event
File the event record with times, volumes, samples, and notifications for the regulator file
Reduce flows and loadings before the event where the plant can store or equalize flow
Return the affected flow to full treatment as soon as the work allows
Monitor the receiving stream and effluent quality through the event as directed
Confirm the maintenance window and the volume and quality expected during the bypass

tasks.explanation: Volume and quality are confirmed before notification, flows are reduced before the event starts, and the filed record closes the event completely.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for an effluent quality audit before a regulator inspection.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: plant prepares for an inspection of effluent performance, records, and sampling practice.

cards.label: Correct any record or equipment gap found and note the correction date
List any exceedance, near miss, or data gap with its cause and corrective action
Check calibration and maintenance records for every effluent monitor and sampler
Compile effluent results for the last two years and compare them with every applicable limit
Prepare the audit summary for the inspection team with the evidence indexed
Walk the sampling points to confirm they match the sampling plan and are accessible

tasks.explanation: Results are compiled before gaps are listed, equipment records are checked with the data, and corrections are dated before the summary is prepared.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for a laboratory quality assurance program for compliance reporting.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: program covers blanks, duplicates, spikes, and calibration checks for the plant laboratory.

cards.label: Set acceptance limits for blanks, duplicates, and spike recovery in the laboratory manual
Trend quality control results monthly to find a method drifting before it fails
Reject or reanalyse any batch whose quality control falls outside its limits
Report the quality control summary with the compliance results each month
List the analyses used for compliance and the quality control check each one requires
Run the quality control set with each batch and record the result beside the samples

tasks.explanation: Checks are listed by analysis before limits are set, batch control guards every result, and monthly trending catches drift before a batch fails.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for preparing the monthly effluent compliance report.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: senior operator compiles the report from sampling, laboratory, and operating records.

cards.label: Check each result for completeness, correct units, and sampling dates
Draft the report with explanations for any exceedance or data gap
Collect all effluent results for the month from the laboratory system
Calculate monthly averages, loadings, and exceedance counts for each parameter
Compare the month with provincial requirements and the federal Wastewater Systems Effluent Regulations limits
Submit the report after senior review and file the signed copy in the plant record

tasks.explanation: Results are checked for completeness before averages are calculated, compliance is judged against both levels of requirements, and senior review precedes submission.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for operating a tertiary effluent filter program.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: deep bed filters polish secondary effluent, filter runs are managed against turbidity and head loss.

cards.label: Run filters to the run end criteria and backwash on the set sequence
Record run lengths and wash water use weekly to track filter performance
Wash and inspect any filter that shortens its run length repeatedly
Set the turbidity target and head loss limit that end a filter run
Confirm filter media condition and backwash system operation at the start of the season
Monitor filtrate turbidity at the start of each run for ripening behaviour

tasks.explanation: Media and backwash readiness come first, run end criteria are fixed before operation, and weekly run records reveal filters that are deteriorating.

tasks.prompt: Order the steps for protecting effluent ammonia compliance during a planned aeration outage.
tasks.assumptions: Fictional western Canadian wastewater treatment scenario for study purposes. In real operations, follow the site procedures, the equipment manuals, and supervisor direction.
tasks.configuration: Scope: one blower must be taken down for a day, nitrification is the compliance risk.

cards.label: Brief shifts on the outage window, sampling plan, and the escalation trigger
Restore normal aeration and wasting in steps once the blower is proven back in service
Sample effluent ammonia every few hours through the outage and log the response
Calculate the oxygen demand the remaining blowers must meet at the planned load
